deities: Ambika Devi (clan goddess/kuldevi of the Katoch dynasty - shrine intact, still actively worshipped; a museum is housed in/near it)
Rishabhanatha/Adinath (Svetambara Jain Tirthankara - Jain temple with a monolithic idol; NOT Hindu - see summary)
festivals: Navratri at the Ambika Devi shrine
Annual collective Jain puja in March at the Jain shrine (inside the fort and at the temple opposite the fort entrance)

history.dynasty: Katoch dynasty of Kangra (fort founded by the legendary Shusharma Chand Katoch); ASI-managed since independence under agreement with Maharaja Jai Chandra's family
history.period: Ancient origins (legendary); fort saw action from Mahmud of Ghazni (1009 AD) to Jahangir (1619/1620); temples' surviving fabric pre-1905, mostly ruined in the 1905 earthquake
history.summary: COMPOSITE ENTRY: 'Kangra Fort Temples' is not one temple but the temple courtyard inside Kangra Fort at Purana Kangra (Old Kangra), about 3 km from Kangra town. Beyond the Darshani Darwaza (gate of worship) stand three stone-carved shrines: Ambika Devi (the Katoch clan goddess; royalkangra.com calls it the oldest Ambika Devi temple in India - claim, verify), Lakshmi-Narayan, and a Svetambara Jain temple. FLAG - JAIN SHRINE INCLUDED: the Jain temple holds an idol of Adinath/Rishabhanatha - a Jain pilgrimage site, not a Hindu temple; keep-or-drop decision needed for that shrine. The idol's age is disputed (ASI: ~550 years / 1446 AD; Jain cult tradition: ancient, linked to Shusharma Chandra's daughter and Neminath, Krishna's cousin). All three temples were completely destroyed in the 1905 Kangra earthquake (magnitude 7.8); the Jain idol reportedly survived undamaged. The Ambika Devi shrine remains in worship - the Katoch family still offers prayers there, and the family retains the temples and parts of the palace courtyards while ASI manages the fort. The fort itself withstood 52 sieges per tradition, was taken by Jahangir, held by Gurkhas (1806), ceded to Ranjit Singh (1809), annexed by the British (1846), garrisoned until the 1905 quake, and is now an ASI ticketed monument with 11 gates and 23 bastions across 463 acres.

name: Kangra Fort Temples
town_description: Kangra (ancient Nagarkot) is a historic town in Himachal Pradesh's Kangra valley, about 20 km from Dharamshala. The fort stands at Purana Kangra (Old Kangra), about 3 km from the town, on a steep rock between the Banganga and Manjhi rivers.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism - Ambika Devi; Vaishnavism - Lakshmi-Narayan), plus one Svetambara Jain shrine (NOT Hindu - flag)

travel.airport: Kangra (Gaggal) Airport is about 13-15 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Kangra station (narrow-gauge Kangra Valley Railway) is about 5 km away; Pathankot is the nearest broad-gauge railhead (~90 km).
travel.road: About 3 km from Kangra town on the Old Kangra road; the climb to the fort passes through seven gates.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; mornings for the climb and valley views.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort open daily; commonly cited 9:00 AM to 5:00/6:00 PM (verify on site). Ticketed ASI monument - confirm current entry fees locally; a museum at the entrance displays pre-1905 photographs and stone sculptures.
